breadth.label: Percent of S&P 500 stocks above 50-day MA
breadth.note: Below 30 bullish, above 70 bearish. Computed by Thaddeus from Yahoo Finance daily closes for 500 of 503 current S&P 500 constituents at the Nov. 20 close (mimics MMFI). Down from 48.9%.

fear_greed.commentary: Fear & Greed plunged to 10, deep in extreme fear, from 19 a prior close and 37 a week ago, as the AI-led rout accelerated; it is the lowest reading in the past month.

markets.summary: A brutal Friday: the S&P 500 fell 3.7% to 6,910.39, its seventh straight loss and lowest close since April, and the Nasdaq sank 5.28% to 22,617.73, turning negative for the year, while the Dow lost 1.93% to 48,147.33. All three are well below their 40-week averages with RSI in the mid-20s, and the S&P is down about 8.6% on the week. Tech was the epicenter, with Nvidia plunging 14% to $125.53 on a report of an SEC accounting probe. Small caps fell too: the Russell 2000 dropped 2.8% to 2,581.79, below its 40-week average. The 10-year Treasury yield eased to about 4.91%. Gold futures fell 4.6% to about $3,515 and silver futures 7.4% to about $41.03, both far below their 40-week averages with RSI near 21 as forced liquidations and Fed rate-hike expectations hit metals. Breadth slipped to 42.8% of S&P 500 stocks above their 50-day average, still neutral, and Fear & Greed is in extreme fear.

stories.headline: Douglas County awards up to $5.95 million contract to start building Macanta Regional Park
stories.summary: Commissioners approved the build contract for the 464-acre park northeast of Castle Rock, with about 5.5 miles of trail and three sets of Incline-style challenge stairs; opening is still targeted for summer 2028.

stories.headline: Crystal Valley Parkway interchange on I-25 fully opens in Castle Rock
stories.summary: The $144.7 million Exit 179 project, the largest in town history and decades in planning, opened to traffic eight months ahead of schedule with a new bridge over I-25 and the BNSF tracks.

stories.headline: Russian strikes on Kyiv kill 3, cripple bridges and cut power
stories.summary: A missile-and-drone barrage hit three Dnipro River bridges and power infrastructure in Kyiv, days after Ukraine struck the Crimean Bridge and Putin vowed retaliation.

stories.headline: Burnham seals trade and youth mobility deals at UK-EU summit
stories.summary: At the Brussels summit, the UK and EU agreed to ease food and drink export checks, link emissions trading and create a youth scheme for up to 100,000 young people each way, the biggest step toward the EU since Brexit.

stories.headline: Anthropic's record IPO closes at $93.5 billion after underwriters exercise greenshoe
stories.summary: Underwriters took up the full over-allotment option, lifting total proceeds of the largest IPO on record to $93.5 billion a day after shares jumped in their Nasdaq debut.

stories.headline: MSU football falls 45-7 to No. 13 Oregon on Senior Day
stories.summary: Freshman QB Kayd Coffman made his second start as the Spartans dropped to 3-8 (1-7 Big Ten); Jaziun Patterson's 1-yard run was MSU's only score.

stories.headline: MSU men's basketball suffers first loss of the season at Tennessee
stories.summary: The Spartans lost 61-46 in Knoxville, their first defeat after a 4-0 start that included a win over Duke; Detroit Mercy visits Saturday.

stories.headline: No. 1 seed MSU women's soccer opens NCAA tournament Saturday vs. CCSU
stories.summary: The third-ranked Spartans host Central Connecticut State at DeMartin Stadium on Saturday afternoon; the men's team is a No. 4 seed in its bracket.

weather.summary: Dangerous, possibly life-threatening flash flooding continues tonight along the east-central and northeast Florida coast (High Risk for the Volusia County coast), as a developing coastal low brings heavy rain, gusty winds, coastal flooding and beach erosion up the Southeast coast this weekend, with rain reaching the Carolinas, Mid-Atlantic and New England; NHC is watching it for possible development. Near-record warmth in the central U.S. and Great Lakes gives way to much colder air behind a strong cold front, while snow continues in parts of the northern Rockies and Intermountain West.
